left-center-right.name: left-center-right
left-center-right.documentation: The left-center-right type is used to define horizontal alignment and text justification.

value.documentation: Left horizontal alignment or justification.
Center horizontal alignment or justification.
Right horizontal alignment or justification.

smufl-coda-glyph-name.name: smufl-coda-glyph-name
smufl-coda-glyph-name.documentation: The smufl-coda-glyph-name type is used to reference a specific Standard Music Font Layout (SMuFL) coda character. The value is a SMuFL canonical glyph name that starts with coda.

font-family.name: font-family
font-family.documentation: The font-family is a comma-separated list of font names. These can be specific font styles such as Maestro or Opus, or one of several generic font styles: music, engraved, handwritten, text, serif, sans-serif, handwritten, cursive, fantasy, and monospace. The music, engraved, and handwritten values refer to music fonts; the rest refer to text fonts. The fantasy style refers to decorative text such as found in older German-style printing.

font-weight.name: font-weight
font-weight.documentation: The font-weight type represents a simplified version of the [CSS font-weight property](https://www.w3.org/TR/2018/REC-css-fonts-3-20180920/#font-prop-desc).

left-right.name: left-right
left-right.documentation: The left-right type is used to indicate whether one element appears to the left or the right of another element.

value.documentation: This element appears to the left of the reference element.
This element appears to the right of the reference element.

line-shape.name: line-shape
line-shape.documentation: The line-shape type distinguishes between straight and curved lines.

line-type.name: line-type
line-type.documentation: The line-type type distinguishes between solid, dashed, dotted, and wavy lines.

effect-value.name: effect-value
effect-value.documentation: The effect-value type represents pictograms for sound effect percussion instruments. The cannon, lotus flute, and megaphone values are in addition to Stone's list.

line-end.name: line-end
line-end.documentation: The line-end type specifies if there is a jog up or down (or both), an arrow, or nothing at the start or end of a bracket.

midi-128.name: midi-128
midi-128.documentation: The midi-128 type is used to express MIDI 1.0 values that range from 1 to 128. MusicXML uses 1-based numbers rather than 0-based numbers often found in MIDI 1.0 documentation.

midi-16.name: midi-16
midi-16.documentation: The midi-16 type is used to express MIDI 1.0 values that range from 1 to 16.

midi-16384.name: midi-16384
midi-16384.documentation: The midi-16384 type is used to express MIDI 1.0 values that range from 1 to 16,384. MusicXML uses 1-based numbers rather than 0-based numbers often found in MIDI 1.0 documentation.

smufl-accidental-glyph-name.name: smufl-accidental-glyph-name
smufl-accidental-glyph-name.documentation: The smufl-accidental-glyph-name type is used to reference a specific Standard Music Font Layout (SMuFL) accidental character. The value is a SMuFL canonical glyph name that starts with one of the strings used at the start of glyph names for SMuFL accidentals.

smufl-pictogram-glyph-name.name: smufl-pictogram-glyph-name
smufl-pictogram-glyph-name.documentation: The smufl-pictogram-glyph-name type is used to reference a specific Standard Music Font Layout (SMuFL) percussion pictogram character. The value is a SMuFL canonical glyph name that starts with pict.

staff-line-position.name: staff-line-position
staff-line-position.documentation: The staff-line-position type indicates the line position on a given staff. Staff lines are numbered from bottom to top, with 1 being the bottom line on a staff. A staff-line-position value can extend beyond the range of the lines on the current staff.

tip-direction.name: tip-direction
tip-direction.documentation: The tip-direction type represents the direction in which the tip of a stick or beater points, using Unicode arrow terminology.

milliseconds.name: milliseconds
milliseconds.documentation: The milliseconds type represents an integral number of milliseconds.

millimeters.name: millimeters
millimeters.documentation: The millimeters type is a number representing millimeters. This is used in the <scaling> element to provide a default scaling from tenths to physical units.

caesura-value.name: caesura-value
caesura-value.documentation: The caesura-value type represents the shape of the caesura sign.

value.documentation: The empty value is equivalent to the normal value.

circular-arrow.name: circular-arrow
circular-arrow.documentation: The circular-arrow type represents the direction in which a circular arrow points, using Unicode arrow terminology.

xlink-actuate.name: xlink:actuate
xlink-actuate.documentation: See the [definition in the XML Linking Language recommendation](https://www.w3.org/TR/xlink11/#link-behaviors).

value.documentation: An application should traverse from the starting resource to the ending resource only on a post-loading event triggered for the purpose of traversal. This is the default value.
An application should traverse to the ending resource immediately on loading the starting resource.

The behavior of an application traversing to the ending resource is unconstrained by this specification. The application should look for other markup present in the link to determine the appropriate behavior.
The behavior of an application traversing to the ending resource is unconstrained by this specification. No other markup is present to help the application determine the appropriate behavior.

yes-no-number.name: yes-no-number
yes-no-number.documentation: The yes-no-number type is used for attributes that can be either boolean or numeric values.

percent.name: percent
percent.documentation: The percent type specifies a percentage from 0 to 100.

up-down.name: up-down
up-down.documentation: The up-down type is used for the direction of arrows and other pointed symbols like vertical accents, indicating which way the tip is pointing.

syllabic.name: syllabic
syllabic.documentation: Lyric hyphenation is indicated by the syllabic type. The single, begin, end, and middle values represent single-syllable words, word-beginning syllables, word-ending syllables, and mid-word syllables, respectively.

tap-hand.name: tap-hand
tap-hand.documentation: The tap-hand type represents the symbol to use for a tap element. The left and right values refer to the SMuFL guitarLeftHandTapping and guitarRightHandTapping glyphs respectively.

xsd-date.name: xs:date
xsd-date.documentation: See the [definition in the W3C XML Schema standard](https://www.w3.org/TR/xmlschema-2/#date).

xml-lang.name: xml:lang
xml-lang.documentation: See the [definition in the W3C Extensible Markup Language recommendation](https://www.w3.org/TR/xml/#sec-lang-tag). Language names come from ISO 639, with optional country subcodes from ISO 3166.

harmon-closed-value.name: harmon-closed-value
harmon-closed-value.documentation: The harmon-closed-value type represents whether the harmon mute is closed, open, or half-open.

over-under.name: over-under
over-under.documentation: The over-under type is used to indicate whether the tips of curved lines such as slurs and ties are overhand (tips down) or underhand (tips up).

value.documentation: Tips of curved lines are overhand (tips down).
Tips of curved lines are underhand (tips up).

positive-integer-or-empty.name: positive-integer-or-empty
positive-integer-or-empty.documentation: The positive-integer-or-empty values can be either a positive integer or an empty string.

smufl-segno-glyph-name.name: smufl-segno-glyph-name
smufl-segno-glyph-name.documentation: The smufl-segno-glyph-name type is used to reference a specific Standard Music Font Layout (SMuFL) segno character. The value is a SMuFL canonical glyph name that starts with segno.

accidental-value.name: accidental-value
accidental-value.documentation: The accidental-value type represents notated accidentals supported by MusicXML. In the MusicXML 2.0 DTD this was a string with values that could be included. The XSD strengthens the data typing to an enumerated list. The quarter- and three-quarters- accidentals are Tartini-style quarter-tone accidentals. The -down and -up accidentals are quarter-tone accidentals that include arrows pointing down or up. The slash- accidentals are used in Turkish classical music. The numbered sharp and flat accidentals are superscripted versions of the accidental signs, used in Turkish folk music. The sori and koron accidentals are microtonal sharp and flat accidentals used in Iranian and Persian music. The other accidental covers accidentals other than those listed here. It is usually used in combination with the smufl attribute to specify a particular Standard Music Font Layout (SMuFL) accidental. The smufl attribute may be used with any accidental value to help specify the appearance of symbols that share the same MusicXML semantics.

value.documentation: Covers accidentals other than those listed here. It is usually used in combination with the smufl attribute to specify a particular Standard Music Font Layout (SMuFL) accidental.

start-stop-discontinue.name: start-stop-discontinue
start-stop-discontinue.documentation: The start-stop-discontinue type is used to specify <ending> types.

value.documentation: Used with the left barline of the first measure in an ending.
Used with the right barline of the last measure in an ending. Indicates the ending mark concludes with a downward jog, as is typical for first endings
Used with the right barline of the last measure in an ending. Indicates there is no downward jog, as is typical for second endings that do not conclude a piece.

glass-value.name: glass-value
glass-value.documentation: The glass-value type represents pictograms for glass percussion instruments.

semi-pitched.name: semi-pitched
semi-pitched.documentation: The semi-pitched type represents categories of indefinite pitch for percussion instruments.

xsd-nonNegativeInteger.name: xs:nonNegativeInteger
xsd-nonNegativeInteger.documentation: See the [definition in the W3C XML Schema standard](https://www.w3.org/TR/xmlschema-2/#nonNegativeInteger).

right-left-middle.name: right-left-middle
right-left-middle.documentation: The right-left-middle type is used to specify barline location.

value.documentation: Right barline.
Left barline.
Mid-measure barline.

pedal-type.name: pedal-type
pedal-type.documentation: The pedal-type distinguishes types of pedal directions.

value.documentation: Indicates the start of a damper pedal.
Indicates a pedal lift without a retake.
Indicates the start of a sostenuto pedal.
Indicates a pedal lift and retake indicated with an inverted V marking. Used when the <pedal> line attribute is yes.
Allows more precise formatting across system breaks and for more complex pedaling lines. Used when the <pedal> line attribute is yes.
Indicates the end of a pedal line that does not include the explicit lift represented by the stop type. Used when the <pedal> line attribute is yes.

Indicates the start of a pedal line that does not include the downstroke represented by the start type. It can be used when a line resumes after being discontinued, or to start a pedal line that is preceded by a text or symbol representation of the pedal. Used when the <pedal> line attribute is yes.

up-down-stop-continue.name: up-down-stop-continue
up-down-stop-continue.documentation: The up-down-stop-continue type is used for octave-shift elements, indicating the direction of the shift from their true pitched values because of printing difficulty.

value.documentation: Start of an <octave-shift> up, such as 8va bassa.
Start of an <octave-shift> down, such as 8va.
Stop of an <octave-shift>.
Continuation of an <octave-shift>, including system breaks.

hole-closed-location.name: hole-closed-location
hole-closed-location.documentation: The hole-closed-location type indicates which portion of the hole is filled in when the corresponding hole-closed-value is half.

group-barline-value.name: group-barline-value
group-barline-value.documentation: The group-barline-value type indicates if the group should have common barlines.

group-symbol-value.name: group-symbol-value
group-symbol-value.documentation: The group-symbol-value type indicates how the symbol for a group or multi-staff part is indicated in the score.

value.documentation: No symbol is displayed.

numeral-value.name: numeral-value
numeral-value.documentation: The numeral-value type represents a Roman numeral or Nashville number value as a positive integer from 1 to 7.

xsd-NMTOKEN.name: xs:NMTOKEN
xsd-NMTOKEN.documentation: See the [definition in the W3C XML Schema standard](https://www.w3.org/TR/xmlschema-2/#NMTOKEN).

smufl-lyrics-glyph-name.name: smufl-lyrics-glyph-name
smufl-lyrics-glyph-name.documentation: The smufl-lyrics-glyph-name type is used to reference a specific Standard Music Font Layout (SMuFL) lyrics elision character. The value is a SMuFL canonical glyph name that starts with lyrics.

xsd-decimal.name: xs:decimal
xsd-decimal.documentation: See the [definition in the W3C XML Schema standard](https://www.w3.org/TR/xmlschema-2/#decimal).

line-length.name: line-length
line-length.documentation: The line-length type distinguishes between different line lengths for doit, falloff, plop, and scoop articulations.

show-tuplet.name: show-tuplet
show-tuplet.documentation: The show-tuplet type indicates whether to show a part of a tuplet relating to the <tuplet-actual> element, both the tuplet-actual and tuplet-normal elements, or neither.

positive-decimal.name: positive-decimal
positive-decimal.documentation: The positive-decimal type specifies a positive decimal value.

smufl-wavy-line-glyph-name.name: smufl-wavy-line-glyph-name
smufl-wavy-line-glyph-name.documentation: The smufl-wavy-line-glyph-name type is used to reference a specific Standard Music Font Layout (SMuFL) wavy line character. The value is a SMuFL canonical glyph name that either starts with wiggle, or begins with guitar and ends with VibratoStroke. This includes all the glyphs in the [Multi-segment lines range](https://www.w3.org/2021/03/smufl14/tables/multi-segment-lines.html), excluding the beam glyphs.

margin-type.name: margin-type
margin-type.documentation: The margin-type type specifies whether margins apply to even page, odd pages, or both.

value.documentation: Margins apply to odd pages only.
Margins apply to even pages only.
Margins apply to both even and odd pages.

positive-divisions.name: positive-divisions
positive-divisions.documentation: The positive-divisions type restricts divisions values to positive numbers.

start-stop-continue.name: start-stop-continue
start-stop-continue.documentation:
The start-stop-continue type is used for an attribute of musical elements that can either start or stop, but also need to refer to an intermediate point in the symbol, as for complex slurs or for formatting of symbols across system breaks.

The values of start, stop, and continue refer to how an element appears in musical score order, not in MusicXML document order. An element with a stop attribute may precede the corresponding element with a start attribute within a MusicXML document. This is particularly common in multi-staff music. For example, the stopping point for a slur may appear in staff 1 before the starting point for the slur appears in staff 2 later in the document.

When multiple elements with the same tag are used within the same note, their order within the MusicXML document should match the musical score order. For example, a note that marks both the end of one slur and the start of a new slur should have the incoming slur element with a type of stop precede the outgoing slur element with a type of start.

value.documentation: Starting point of an element.
Stopping point of an element.
Continuation of an element, including system breaks.

xsd-language.name: xs:language
xsd-language.documentation: See the [definition in the W3C XML Schema standard](https://www.w3.org/TR/xmlschema-2/#language).

symbol-size.name: symbol-size
symbol-size.documentation: The symbol-size type is used to distinguish between full, cue sized, grace cue sized, and oversized symbols.

value.documentation: Use a full-sized symbol.
Use a cue-sized symbol, generally smaller than a full-sized symbol.
Use a grace-cue-sized symbol, generally smaller than a cue-sized symbol.
Use an oversized symbol.

valign-image.name: valign-image
valign-image.documentation: The valign-image type is used to indicate vertical alignment for images and graphics, so it does not include a baseline value. Defaults are implementation-dependent.

value.documentation: Aligned to the top of the image.
Aligned to the middle of the image.
Aligned to the bottom of the image.

xsd-integer.name: xs:integer
xsd-integer.documentation: See the [definition in the W3C XML Schema standard](https://www.w3.org/TR/xmlschema-2/#integer).

membrane-value.name: membrane-value
membrane-value.documentation: The membrane-value type represents pictograms for membrane percussion instruments.

staff-line.name: staff-line
staff-line.documentation: The staff-line type indicates the line on a given staff. Staff lines are numbered from bottom to top, with 1 being the bottom line on a staff.

staff-type.name: staff-type
staff-type.documentation: The staff-type value specifies different uses for the staff.

value.documentation: An ossia staff represents music that can be played instead of what appears on the regular staff.
An editorial staff represents musical alternatives created by an editor rather than the composer. It can be used for suggested interpretations or alternatives from other sources.
A cue staff represents music from another part.

An alternate staff shares the same music as the prior staff, but displayed differently (e.g., treble and bass clef, standard notation and tablature). It is not included in playback. An alternate staff provides more information to an application reading a file than encoding the same music in separate parts, so its use is preferred in this situation if feasible.
A regular staff is the standard default staff-type.

start-note.name: start-note
start-note.documentation: The start-note type describes the starting note of trills and mordents for playback, relative to the current note.

start-stop.name: start-stop
start-stop.documentation:
The start-stop type is used for an attribute of musical elements that can either start or stop, such as tuplets.

The values of start and stop refer to how an element appears in musical score order, not in MusicXML document order. An element with a stop attribute may precede the corresponding element with a start attribute within a MusicXML document. This is particularly common in multi-staff music. For example, the stopping point for a tuplet may appear in staff 1 before the starting point for the tuplet appears in staff 2 later in the document.

When multiple elements with the same tag are used within the same note, their order within the MusicXML document should match the musical score order.

value.documentation: Starting point of an element.
Stopping point of an element.

stem-value.name: stem-value
stem-value.documentation: The stem-value type represents the notated stem direction.

value.documentation: No stem appears.

stick-type.name: stick-type
stick-type.documentation: The stick-type type represents the shape of pictograms where the material in the stick, mallet, or beater is represented in the pictogram.

staff-divide-symbol.name: staff-divide-symbol
staff-divide-symbol.documentation: The staff-divide-symbol type is used for staff division symbols. The down, up, and up-down values correspond to SMuFL code points U+E00B, U+E00C, and U+E00D respectively.

tied-type.name: tied-type
tied-type.documentation:
The tied-type type is used as an attribute of the tied element to specify where the visual representation of a tie begins and ends. A <tied> element which joins two notes of the same pitch can be specified with tied-type start on the first note and tied-type stop on the second note. To indicate a note should be undamped, use a single <tied> element with tied-type let-ring. For other ties that are visually attached to a single note, such as a tie leading into or out of a repeated section or coda, use two <tied> elements on the same note, one start and one stop.

In start-stop cases, ties can add more elements using a continue type. This is typically used to specify the formatting of cross-system ties.

value.documentation: Start of a tie.
End of a tie.
Continuation of a tie, usually used for cross-system formatting.
A tie that indicates an instrument should be undamped.

beam-level.name: beam-level
beam-level.documentation: The MusicXML format supports six levels of beaming, up to 1024th notes. Unlike the number-level type, the beam-level type identifies concurrent beams in a beam group. It does not distinguish overlapping beams such as grace notes within regular notes, or beams used in different voices.

beam-value.name: beam-value
beam-value.documentation: The beam-value type represents the type of beam associated with each of 8 beam levels (up to 1024th notes) available for each note.

smufl-glyph-name.name: smufl-glyph-name
smufl-glyph-name.documentation: The smufl-glyph-name type is used for attributes that reference a specific Standard Music Font Layout (SMuFL) character. The value is a SMuFL canonical glyph name, not a code point. For instance, the value for a standard piano pedal mark would be keyboardPedalPed, not U+E650.

pitched-value.name: pitched-value
pitched-value.documentation: The pitched-value type represents pictograms for pitched percussion instruments. The chimes and tubular chimes values distinguish the single-line and double-line versions of the pictogram.

time-only.name: time-only
time-only.documentation: The time-only type is used to indicate that a particular playback- or listening-related element only applies particular times through a repeated section. The value is a comma-separated list of positive integers arranged in ascending order, indicating which times through the repeated section that the element applies.

top-bottom.name: top-bottom
top-bottom.documentation: The top-bottom type is used to indicate the top or bottom part of a vertical shape like non-arpeggiate.

value.documentation: Top of the vertical shape.
Bottom of the vertical shape.

trill-step.name: trill-step
trill-step.documentation: The trill-step type describes the alternating note of trills and mordents for playback, relative to the current note.

sync-type.name: sync-type
sync-type.documentation: The sync-type type specifies the style that a score following application should use to synchronize an accompaniment with a performer.

value.documentation: No synchronization to the performer.
Synchronization is based on the performer tempo rather than individual events in the score.
Combines the tempo and event approaches, giving more weight to tempo.
Combines the tempo and event approaches, giving more weight to performed events.
Synchronization follows the performance of individual events in the score rather than the performer tempo.
Provides the strictest synchronization by not being forgiving of missing performed events.

show-frets.name: show-frets
show-frets.documentation: The show-frets type indicates whether to show tablature frets as numbers (0, 1, 2) or letters (a, b, c). The default choice is numbers.

semitones.name: semitones
semitones.documentation: The semitones type is a number representing semitones, used for chromatic alteration. A value of -1 corresponds to a flat and a value of 1 to a sharp. Decimal values like 0.5 (quarter tone sharp) are used for microtones.

metal-value.name: metal-value
metal-value.documentation: The metal-value type represents pictograms for metal percussion instruments. The hi-hat value refers to a pictogram like high-hat cymbals, but without the long vertical line at the bottom.

system-relation.name: system-relation
system-relation.documentation: The system-relation type distinguishes elements that are associated with a system rather than the particular part where the element appears.

value.documentation: The element should appear only on the top part of the current system.

The element should appear on both the current part and the top part of the current system. If this value appears in a score, when parts are created the element should only appear once in this part, not twice.
The element is associated only with the current part, not with the system.

note-size-type.name: note-size-type
note-size-type.documentation: The note-size-type type indicates the type of note size being defined by a <note-size> element.

value.documentation: The cue type is used for notes of cue size that do not include a <grace> element, whether defined explicitly or implicitly via a <cue> element.
The grace type is used for notes of cue size that include a <grace> element.
The grace-cue type is used for notes of grace-cue size.
The large type is used for notes of large size.

bend-shape.name: bend-shape
bend-shape.documentation: The bend-shape type distinguishes between the angled bend symbols commonly used in standard notation and the curved bend symbols commonly used in both tablature and standard notation.

measure-text.name: measure-text
measure-text.documentation: The measure-text type is used for the text attribute of measure elements. It has at least one character. The implicit attribute of the measure element should be set to "yes" rather than setting the text attribute to an empty string.

degree-symbol-value.name: degree-symbol-value
degree-symbol-value.documentation: The degree-symbol-value type indicates which symbol should be used in specifying a degree.

bar-style.name: bar-style
bar-style.documentation: The bar-style type represents barline style information. Choices are regular, dotted, dashed, heavy, light-light, light-heavy, heavy-light, heavy-heavy, tick (a short stroke through the top line), short (a partial barline between the 2nd and 4th lines), and none.

value.documentation: No barline appears.

principal-voice-symbol.name: principal-voice-symbol
principal-voice-symbol.documentation: The principal-voice-symbol type represents the type of symbol used to indicate a principal or secondary voice.

value.documentation:  if the type is start,  if the type is stop.
Used for analysis markup when the <principal-voice> element does not have a corresponding appearance in the score.

arrow-style.name: arrow-style
arrow-style.documentation: The arrow-style type represents the style of an arrow, using Unicode arrow terminology. Filled and hollow arrows indicate polygonal single arrows. Paired arrows are duplicate single arrows in the same direction. Combined arrows apply to double direction arrows like left right, indicating that an arrow in one direction should be combined with an arrow in the other direction.

value.documentation: Another style besides one of those listed.

ending-number.name: ending-number
ending-number.documentation: The ending-number type is used to specify either a comma-separated list of positive integers without leading zeros, or a string of zero or more spaces. It is used for the number attribute of the <ending> element. The zero or more spaces version is used when software knows that an ending is present, but cannot determine the type of the ending.

arrow-direction.name: arrow-direction
arrow-direction.documentation: The arrow-direction type represents the direction in which an arrow points, using Unicode arrow terminology.

value.documentation: Another direction besides one of those listed.

xsd-positiveInteger.name: xs:positiveInteger
xsd-positiveInteger.documentation: See the [definition in the W3C XML Schema standard](https://www.w3.org/TR/xmlschema-2/#positiveInteger).

clef-sign.name: clef-sign
clef-sign.documentation: The clef-sign type represents the different clef symbols.

value.documentation: The TAB sign indicates that the music that follows should be in tablature notation.
The jianpu sign indicates that the music that follows should be in jianpu numbered notation. Unlike TAB, a jianpu sign does not correspond to a visual clef notation.
Deprecated as of MusicXML 4.0. Use the clef element's print-object attribute instead. When the none sign is used, notes should be displayed as if in treble clef.

backward-forward.name: backward-forward
backward-forward.documentation: The backward-forward type is used to specify repeat directions. The start of the repeat has a forward direction while the end of the repeat has a backward direction.

system-relation-number.name: system-relation-number
system-relation-number.documentation: The system-relation-number type distinguishes measure numbers that are associated with a system rather than the particular part where the element appears.

value.documentation: The number should appear only on the top part of the current system.
The number should appear only on the bottom part of the current system.

The number should appear on both the current part and the top part of the current system. If these values appear in a score, when parts are created the number should only appear once in this part, not twice.

The number should appear on both the current part and the bottom part of the current system. If these values appear in a score, when parts are created the number should only appear once in this part, not twice.
The number is associated only with the current part, not with the system.

stick-location.name: stick-location
stick-location.documentation: The stick-location type represents pictograms for the location of sticks, beaters, or mallets on cymbals, gongs, drums, and other instruments.

stick-material.name: stick-material
stick-material.documentation: The stick-material type represents the material being displayed in a stick pictogram.

distance-type.name: distance-type
distance-type.documentation:
The distance-type defines what type of distance is being defined in a <distance> element. Values include:

- beam
- hyphen

This is left as a string so that other application-specific types can be defined, but it is made a separate type so that it can be redefined more strictly.

The beam type represents the distance between beams. The hyphen type represents the distance between hyphens in lyrics.

breath-mark-value.name: breath-mark-value
breath-mark-value.documentation: The breath-mark-value type represents the symbol used for a breath mark.

value.documentation: The exact symbol used is application-dependent.

line-width-type.name: line-width-type
line-width-type.documentation:
The line-width-type defines what type of line is being defined in a <line-width> element. Values include:

- beam
- bracket
- dashes
- enclosure
- ending
- extend
- heavy barline
- leger
- light barline
- octave shift
- pedal
- slur middle
- slur tip
- staff
- stem
- tie middle
- tie tip
- tuplet bracket
- wedge

This is left as a string so that other application-specific types can be defined, but it is made a separate type so that it can be redefined more strictly.

tremolo-type.name: tremolo-type
tremolo-type.documentation: The tremolo-type is used to distinguish double-note, single-note, and unmeasured tremolos.

value.documentation: Start of a double-note tremolo.
Stop of a double-note tremolo.
Single-note tremolo.
Unmeasured tremolo.

note-type-value.name: note-type-value
note-type-value.documentation: The note-type-value type is used for the MusicXML type element and represents the graphic note type, from 1024th (shortest) to maxima (longest).

divisions.name: divisions
divisions.documentation: The divisions type is used to express values in terms of the musical divisions defined by the divisions element. It is preferred that these be integer values both for MIDI interoperability and to avoid roundoff errors.

xsd-string.name: xs:string
xsd-string.documentation: See the [definition in the W3C XML Schema standard](https://www.w3.org/TR/xmlschema-2/#string).

xsd-token.name: xs:token
xsd-token.documentation: See the [definition in the W3C XML Schema standard](https://www.w3.org/TR/xmlschema-2/#token).

fermata-shape.name: fermata-shape
fermata-shape.documentation: The fermata-shape type represents the shape of the fermata sign. The empty value is equivalent to the normal value.

value.documentation: The empty value is equivalent to the normal value.

number-of-lines.name: number-of-lines
number-of-lines.documentation: The number-of-lines type is used to specify the number of lines in text decoration attributes.

rotation-degrees.name: rotation-degrees
rotation-degrees.documentation: The rotation-degrees type specifies rotation, pan, and elevation values in degrees. Values range from -180 to 180.

text-direction.name: text-direction
text-direction.documentation: The text-direction type is used to adjust and override the Unicode bidirectional text algorithm, similar to the Directionality data category in the [W3C Internationalization Tag Set recommendation](https://www.w3.org/TR/2007/REC-its-20070403/#directionality).

value.documentation: Left-to-right embed.
Right-to-left embed.
Left-to-right bidi-override.
Right-to-left bidi-override.

harmony-arrangement.name: harmony-arrangement
harmony-arrangement.documentation: The harmony-arrangement type indicates how stacked chords and bass notes are displayed within a harmony element. The vertical value specifies that the second element appears below the first. The horizontal value specifies that the second element appears to the right of the first. The diagonal value specifies that the second element appears both below and to the right of the first.

staff-number.name: staff-number
staff-number.documentation: The staff-number type indicates staff numbers within a multi-staff part. Staves are numbered from top to bottom, with 1 being the top staff on a part.

upright-inverted.name: upright-inverted
upright-inverted.documentation: The upright-inverted type describes the appearance of a fermata element. The value is upright if not specified.

beater-value.name: beater-value
beater-value.documentation: The beater-value type represents pictograms for beaters, mallets, and sticks that do not have different materials represented in the pictogram.

xlink-href.name: xlink:href
xlink-href.documentation: See the [definition in the XML Linking Language recommendation](https://www.w3.org/TR/xlink11/#link-locators).

xlink-type.name: xlink:type
xlink-type.documentation: See the [definition in the XML Linking Language recommendation](https://www.w3.org/TR/xlink11/#link-types). MusicXML only supports the simple type.

value.documentation: See the [definition in the XML Linking Language recommendation](https://www.w3.org/TR/xlink11/#dt-simplelink).

xlink-role.name: xlink:role
xlink-role.documentation: See the [definition in the XML Linking Language recommendation](https://www.w3.org/TR/xlink11/#link-semantics).

xlink-show.name: xlink:show
xlink-show.documentation: See the [definition in the XML Linking Language recommendation](https://www.w3.org/TR/xlink11/#link-behaviors).

value.documentation: An application traversing to the ending resource should load it in a new window, frame, pane, or other relevant presentation context.

An application traversing to the ending resource should load the resource in the same window, frame, pane, or other relevant presentation context in which the starting resource was loaded. This is the default value.
An application traversing to the ending resource should load its presentation in place of the presentation of the starting resource.

The behavior of an application traversing to the ending resource is unconstrained by this specification. The application should look for other markup present in the link to determine the appropriate behavior.
The behavior of an application traversing to the ending resource is unconstrained by this specification. No other markup is present to help the application determine the appropriate behavior.

degree-type-value.name: degree-type-value
degree-type-value.documentation: The degree-type-value type indicates whether the current degree element is an addition, alteration, or subtraction to the kind of the current chord in the harmony element.

value.documentation: If the degree element is in addition to the kind of the current chord.
If the degree element is an alteration to the kind of the current chord.
If the degree element is a subtraction from the kind of the current chord.

wedge-type.name: wedge-type
wedge-type.documentation: The wedge-type type is used to specify <wedge> types.

value.documentation: Start of a crescendo <wedge> that is closed on the left side.
Start of a diminuendo <wedge> that is closed on the right side.
Stop of a <wedge>.
Continuation of a <wedge>, including system breaks.

xlink-title.name: xlink:title
xlink-title.documentation: See the [definition in the XML Linking Language recommendation](https://www.w3.org/TR/xlink11/#link-semantics).

wood-value.name: wood-value
wood-value.documentation: The wood-value type represents pictograms for wood percussion instruments. The maraca and maracas values distinguish the one- and two-maraca versions of the pictogram.

notehead-value.name: notehead-value
notehead-value.documentation:
The notehead-value type indicates shapes other than the open and closed ovals associated with note durations.

The values do, re, mi, fa, fa up, so, la, and ti correspond to Aikin's 7-shape system. The fa up shape is typically used with upstems; the fa shape is typically used with downstems or no stems.

The arrow shapes differ from triangle and inverted triangle by being centered on the stem. Slashed and back slashed notes include both the normal notehead and a slash. The triangle shape has the tip of the triangle pointing up; the inverted triangle shape has the tip of the triangle pointing down. The left triangle shape is a right triangle with the hypotenuse facing up and to the left.

The other notehead covers noteheads other than those listed here. It is usually used in combination with the smufl attribute to specify a particular SMuFL notehead. The smufl attribute may be used with any notehead value to help specify the appearance of symbols that share the same MusicXML semantics. Noteheads in the SMuFL Note name noteheads and Note name noteheads supplement ranges (U+E150–U+E1AF and U+EEE0–U+EEFF) should not use the smufl attribute or the "other" value, but instead use the notehead-text element.

value.documentation: As in Aikin's 7-shape system.
As in Aikin's 7-shape system.
As in Aikin's 7-shape system.
As in Aikin's 7-shape system, typically used with downstems or no stems.
As in Aikin's 7-shape system, typically used with upstems.
As in Aikin's 7-shape system.
As in Aikin's 7-shape system.
As in Aikin's 7-shape system.

Noteheads other than those listed here. This value is usually used in combination with the smufl attribute to specify a particular SMuFL notehead. The smufl attribute may also be used with any notehead value to help specify the appearance of symbols that share the same MusicXML semantics. Noteheads in the SMuFL Note name noteheads and Note name noteheads supplement ranges (U+E150–U+E1AF and U+EEE0–U+EEFF) should not use the smufl attribute or the other value, but instead use the <notehead-text> element.

xsd-IDREF.name: xs:IDREF
xsd-IDREF.documentation: See the [definition in the W3C XML Schema standard](https://www.w3.org/TR/xmlschema-2/#IDREF).

xsd-NCName.name: xs:NCName
xsd-NCName.documentation: See the [definition in the W3C XML Schema standard](https://www.w3.org/TR/xmlschema-2/#NCName).

xsd-anyURI.name: xs:anyURI
xsd-anyURI.documentation: See the [definition in the W3C XML Schema standard](https://www.w3.org/TR/xmlschema-2/#anyURI).

xml-space.name: xml:space
xml-space.documentation: See the [definition in the W3C Extensible Markup Language recommendation](https://www.w3.org/TR/xml/#sec-white-space).

font-size.name: font-size
font-size.documentation: The font-size can be one of the [CSS font sizes](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-fonts-3/#font-size-prop) or a decimal point size.

font-style.name: font-style
font-style.documentation: The font-style type represents a simplified version of the [CSS font-style property](https://www.w3.org/TR/2018/REC-css-fonts-3-20180920/#font-prop-desc).

above-below.name: above-below
above-below.documentation: The above-below type is used to indicate whether one element appears above or below another element.

value.documentation: This element appears above the reference element.
This element appears below the reference element.

number-or-normal.name: number-or-normal
number-or-normal.documentation: The number-or-normal values can be either a decimal number or the string "normal". This is used by the line-height and letter-spacing attributes.

start-stop-single.name: start-stop-single
start-stop-single.documentation:
The start-stop-single type is used for an attribute of musical elements that can be used for either multi-note or single-note musical elements, as for groupings.

When multiple elements with the same tag are used within the same note, their order within the MusicXML document should match the musical score order.

value.documentation: Starting point of a multi-note element.
Stopping point of a multi-note element.
Single-note element.

handbell-value.name: handbell-value
handbell-value.documentation: The handbell-value type represents the type of handbell technique being notated.

comma-separated-text.name: comma-separated-text
comma-separated-text.documentation: The comma-separated-text type is used to specify a comma-separated list of text elements, as is used by the font-family attribute.

glyph-type.name: glyph-type
glyph-type.documentation:
The glyph-type defines what type of glyph is being defined in a <glyph> element. Values include:

- quarter-rest
- g-clef-ottava-bassa
- c-clef
- f-clef
- percussion-clef
- octave-shift-up-8
- octave-shift-down-8
- octave-shift-continue-8
- octave-shift-down-15
- octave-shift-up-15
- octave-shift-continue-15
- octave-shift-down-22
- octave-shift-up-22
- octave-shift-continue-22

This is left as a string so that other application-specific types can be defined, but it is made a separate type so that it can be redefined more strictly.

A quarter-rest type specifies the glyph to use when a note has a <rest> element and a <type> value of quarter.

The c-clef, f-clef, and percussion-clef types specify the glyph to use when a clef <sign> element value is C, F, or percussion respectively.

The g-clef-ottava-bassa type specifies the glyph to use when a clef <sign> element value is G and the <clef-octave-change> element value is -1.

The octave-shift types specify the glyph to use when an <octave-shift> type attribute value is up, down, or continue and the <octave-shift> size attribute value is 8, 15, or 22.

non-negative-decimal.name: non-negative-decimal
non-negative-decimal.documentation: The non-negative-decimal type specifies a non-negative decimal value.

yyyy-mm-dd.name: yyyy-mm-dd
yyyy-mm-dd.documentation: Calendar dates are represented yyyy-mm-dd format, following [ISO 8601](https://www.iso.org/iso-8601-date-and-time-format.html). This is a W3C XML Schema date type, but without the optional timezone data.

number-level.name: number-level
number-level.documentation:
Slurs, tuplets, and many other features can be concurrent and overlap within a single musical part. The number-level entity distinguishes up to 16 concurrent objects of the same type when the objects overlap in MusicXML document order. Values greater than 6 are usually only needed for music with a large number of divisi staves in a single part, or if there are more than 6 cross-staff arpeggios in a single measure. When a number-level value is optional and has no default value, it is 1 if not specified.

When polyphonic parts are involved, the ordering within a MusicXML document can differ from musical score order. As an example, say we have a piano part in 4/4 where within a single measure, all the notes on the top staff are followed by all the notes on the bottom staff. In this example, each staff has a slur that starts on beat 2 and stops on beat 3, and there is a third slur that goes from beat 1 of one staff to beat 4 of the other staff.

In this situation, the two mid-measure slurs can use the same number because they do not overlap in MusicXML document order, even though they do overlap in musical score order. Within the MusicXML document, the top staff slur will both start and stop before the bottom staff slur starts and stops.

If the cross-staff slur starts in the top staff and stops in the bottom staff, it will need a separate number from the mid-measure slurs because it overlaps those slurs in MusicXML document order. However, if the cross-staff slur starts in the bottom staff and stops in the top staff, all three slurs can use the same number. None of them overlap within the MusicXML document, even though they all overlap each other in the musical score order. Within the MusicXML document, the start and stop of the top-staff slur will be followed by the stop and start of the cross-staff slur, followed by the start and stop of the bottom-staff slur.

As this example demonstrates, a reading program should be prepared to handle cases where the number-levels start and stop in an arbitrary order. Because the start and stop values refer to musical score order, a program may find the stopping point of an object earlier in the MusicXML document than it will find its starting point.

accordion-middle.name: accordion-middle
accordion-middle.documentation: The accordion-middle type may have values of 1, 2, or 3, corresponding to having 1 to 3 dots in the middle section of the accordion registration symbol. This type is not used if no dots are present.

enclosure-shape.name: enclosure-shape
enclosure-shape.documentation: The enclosure-shape type describes the shape and presence / absence of an enclosure around text or symbols. A bracket enclosure is similar to a rectangle with the bottom line missing, as is common in jazz notation. An inverted-bracket enclosure is similar to a rectangle with the top line missing.

value.documentation: No enclosure is displayed.

start-stop-change-continue.name: start-stop-change-continue
start-stop-change-continue.documentation: The start-stop-change-continue type is used to distinguish types of pedal directions.

numeral-mode.name: numeral-mode
numeral-mode.documentation: The numeral-mode type specifies the mode similar to the mode type, but with a restricted set of values. The different minor values are used to interpret <numeral-root> values of 6 and 7 when present in a minor key. The harmonic minor value sharpens the 7 and the melodic minor value sharpens both 6 and 7. If a minor mode is used without qualification, either in the <mode> or <numeral-mode> elements, natural minor is used.

value.documentation: Numerals are interpreted relative to a major scale.
Numerals are interpreted relative to a natural minor scale.
Numerals are interpreted relative to a natural minor scale.
Numerals are interpreted relative to an ascending melodic minor scale with raised 6th and 7th degrees.
Numerals are interpreted relative to a harmonic minor scale with a raised 7th degree.

trill-beats.name: trill-beats
trill-beats.documentation: The trill-beats type specifies the beats used in a trill-sound or bend-sound attribute group. It is a decimal value with a minimum value of 2.

time-separator.name: time-separator
time-separator.documentation: The time-separator type indicates how to display the arrangement between the beats and beat-type values in a time signature. The default value is none. The horizontal, diagonal, and vertical values represent horizontal, diagonal lower-left to upper-right, and vertical lines respectively. For these values, the beats and beat-type values are arranged on either side of the separator line. The none value represents no separator with the beats and beat-type arranged vertically. The adjacent value represents no separator with the beats and beat-type arranged horizontally.

time-relation.name: time-relation
time-relation.documentation: The time-relation type indicates the symbol used to represent the interchangeable aspect of dual time signatures.

tremolo-marks.name: tremolo-marks
tremolo-marks.documentation: The number of tremolo marks is represented by a number from 0 to 8: the same as beam-level with 0 added.

harmony-type.name: harmony-type
harmony-type.documentation: The harmony-type type differentiates different types of harmonies when alternate harmonies are possible. Explicit harmonies have all notes present in the music; implied have some notes missing but implied; alternate represents alternate analyses.

value.documentation: All notes present in the music.
Some notes are missing but implied.
Alternate analysis.

measure-numbering-value.name: measure-numbering-value
measure-numbering-value.documentation: The measure-numbering-value type describes how measure numbers are displayed on this part: no numbers, numbers every measure, or numbers every system.

harmon-closed-location.name: harmon-closed-location
harmon-closed-location.documentation: The harmon-closed-location type indicates which portion of the symbol is filled in when the corresponding harmon-closed-value is half.

swing-type-value.name: swing-type-value
swing-type-value.documentation: The swing-type-value type specifies the note type, either eighth or 16th, to which the ratio defined in the <swing> element is applied.

value.documentation: The <swing> ratio applies to 16th notes.
The <swing> ratio applies to eighth notes.

color.name: color
color.documentation:
The color type indicates the color of an element. Color may be represented as hexadecimal RGB triples, as in HTML, or as hexadecimal ARGB tuples, with the A indicating alpha of transparency. An alpha value of 00 is totally transparent; FF is totally opaque. If RGB is used, the A value is assumed to be FF.

For instance, the RGB value "#800080" represents purple. An ARGB value of "#40800080" would be a transparent purple.

As in [SVG 1.1](https://www.w3.org/TR/SVG11/color.html), colors are defined in terms of the [sRGB color space (IEC 61966)](https://www.color.org/srgb04.xalter).

css-font-size.name: css-font-size
css-font-size.documentation: The css-font-size type includes the [CSS font sizes](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-fonts-3/#font-size-prop) used as an alternative to a numeric point size. In CSS these refer to an entry in a table of font sizes computed and kept by the user agent. The scaling is relative to the reference value of medium.

value.documentation: Scaling factor guideline: 3/5 of medium.
Scaling factor guideline: 3/4 of medium.
Scaling factor guideline: 8/9 of medium.
Scaling factor guideline: equal to medium.
Scaling factor guideline: 6/5 of medium.
Scaling factor guideline: 3/2 of medium.
Scaling factor guideline: 2/1 of medium.

valign.name: valign
valign.documentation: The valign type is used to indicate vertical alignment to the top, middle, bottom, or baseline of the text. If the text is on multiple lines, baseline alignment refers to the baseline of the lowest line of text. Defaults are implementation-dependent.

value.documentation: Aligned to the top of the text.
Aligned to the middle of the text.
Aligned to the bottom of the text.
Aligned to the baseline of the text. If the text is on multiple lines, aligned to the baseline of the lowest line of text.

kind-value.name: kind-value
kind-value.documentation: A kind-value indicates the type of chord. Degree elements can then add, subtract, or alter from these starting points. The 11th and 13th values are usually used as a basis for alteration.

value.documentation: Triad: major third, perfect fifth.
Triad: minor third, perfect fifth.
Triad: major third, augmented fifth.
Triad: minor third, diminished fifth.
Seventh: major triad, minor seventh.
Seventh: major triad, major seventh.
Seventh: minor triad, minor seventh.
Seventh: diminished triad, diminished seventh.
Seventh: augmented triad, minor seventh.
Seventh: diminished triad, minor seventh.
Seventh: minor triad, major seventh.
Sixth: major triad, added sixth.
Sixth: minor triad, added sixth.
Ninth: dominant, major ninth.
Ninth: major-seventh, major ninth.
Ninth: minor-seventh, major ninth.
11th: dominant-ninth, perfect 11th.
11th: major-ninth, perfect 11th.
11th: minor-ninth, perfect 11th.
13th: dominant-11th, major 13th.
13th: major-11th, major 13th.
13th: minor-11th, major 13th.
Suspended: major second, perfect fifth.
Suspended: perfect fourth, perfect fifth.
Functional Neapolitan sixth.
Functional Italian sixth.
Functional French sixth.
Functional German sixth.
Pedal-point bass.
Perfect fifth.
Augmented fourth, augmented sixth, augmented ninth.
Used when the harmony is entirely composed of add elements.

Used to explicitly encode the absence of chords or functional harmony. In this case, the <root> <numeral>, or <function> element has no meaning. When using the <root> or <numeral> element, the <root-step> or <numeral-step> text attribute should be set to the empty string to keep the root or numeral from being displayed.

mute.name: mute
mute.documentation: The mute type represents muting playback for different instruments, including brass, winds, and strings. The on and off values are used for undifferentiated mutes. The remaining values represent specific mutes.

mode.name: mode
mode.documentation: The mode type is used to specify major/minor and other mode distinctions. Valid mode values include major, minor, dorian, phrygian, lydian, mixolydian, aeolian, ionian, locrian, and none.

string-number.name: string-number
string-number.documentation: The string-number type indicates a string number. Strings are numbered from high to low, with 1 being the highest pitched full-length string.

tenths.name: tenths
tenths.documentation:
The tenths type is a number representing tenths of interline staff space (positive or negative). Both integer and decimal values are allowed, such as 5 for a half space and 2.5 for a quarter space. Interline space is measured from the middle of a staff line.

Distances in a MusicXML file are measured in tenths of staff space. Tenths are then scaled to millimeters within the scaling element, used in the defaults element at the start of a score. Individual staves can apply a scaling factor to adjust staff size.

When a MusicXML element or attribute refers to tenths, it means the global tenths defined by the <scaling> element, not the local tenths as adjusted by the <staff-size> element.

two-note-turn.name: two-note-turn
two-note-turn.documentation: The two-note-turn type describes the ending notes of trills and mordents for playback, relative to the current note.

yes-no.name: yes-no
yes-no.documentation: The yes-no type is used for boolean-like attributes. We cannot use W3C XML Schema booleans due to their restrictions on expression of boolean values.

value.documentation: True.
False.

cancel-location.name: cancel-location
cancel-location.documentation: The cancel-location type is used to indicate where a key signature cancellation appears relative to a new key signature: to the left, to the right, or before the barline and to the left. It is left by default. For mid-measure key elements, a cancel-location of before-barline should be treated like a cancel-location of left.

fifths.name: fifths
fifths.documentation: The fifths type represents the number of flats or sharps in a traditional key signature. Negative numbers are used for flats and positive numbers for sharps, reflecting the key's placement within the circle of fifths (hence the type name).

fan.name: fan
fan.documentation: The fan type represents the type of beam fanning present on a note, used to represent accelerandos and ritardandos.

value.documentation: No fanning present.

time-symbol.name: time-symbol
time-symbol.documentation: The time-symbol type indicates how to display a time signature. The normal value is the usual fractional display, and is the implied symbol type if none is specified. Other options are the common and cut time symbols, as well as a single number with an implied denominator. The note symbol indicates that the <beat-type> should be represented with the corresponding downstem note rather than a number. The dotted-note symbol indicates that the <beat-type> should be represented with a dotted downstem note that corresponds to three times the <beat-type> value, and a numerator that is one third the <beats> value.

winged.name: winged
winged.documentation: The winged attribute indicates whether the repeat has winged extensions that appear above and below the barline. The straight and curved values represent single wings, while the double-straight and double-curved values represent double wings. The none value indicates no wings and is the default.

on-off.name: on-off
on-off.documentation: The on-off type is used for notation elements such as string mutes.

octave.name: octave
octave.documentation: Octaves are represented by the numbers 0 to 9, where 4 indicates the octave started by middle C.

hole-closed-value.name: hole-closed-value
hole-closed-value.documentation: The hole-closed-value type represents whether the hole is closed, open, or half-open.

step.name: step
step.documentation: The step type represents a step of the diatonic scale, represented using the English letters A through G.

xsd-ID.name: xs:ID
xsd-ID.documentation: See the [definition in the W3C XML Schema standard](https://www.w3.org/TR/xmlschema-2/#ID).
